premises.text: People have lost control over their digital life and data.
premises.evidence_span: we have unknowingly relinquished real control of our digital life

premises.text: Publicly available information can lead to significant personal issues.
premises.evidence_span: a lot of information about her is currently publicly available because she doesn't understand it

premises.text: Storage of digital content is cheap and permanent.
premises.evidence_span: Storage is cheap, it is everywhere, and it is forever

premises.text: Social Fortress allows users to control their data across various applications.
premises.evidence_span: Because the doctors are using social fortress, and so is the hospital. They're in control of their data

premises.text: Social Fortress is user-friendly enough for non-technical users.
premises.evidence_span: Social fortress is so easy, even my mother can use it

premises.text: Social Fortress provides real-time protection for data across platforms.
premises.evidence_span: Social Fortress works for the enterprise, it works for mobile, it works for the consumer, and it works real time

premises.text: Current security measures are inadequate for protecting data.
premises.evidence_span: we are not a VPN. We are not a single sign-on. We are not DeFactor Authentication. We are not DRM. We are not MDM. And we are not an encryption gateway

premises.text: Users need comprehensive data protection regardless of location or device.
premises.evidence_span: you need Jason Bourne standing with your data no matter where it goes, anywhere in the world, on any device, on any platform, and on any application

value.text: Users regain control over their digital data and content.
value.evidence_span: Welcome to a world with social fortress

notes: Examples of personal data issues and the need for control are emphasized.
